faq.q1: Does the platform write my thesis for me?
faq.a1: No — and it will tell you so. It structures the work, drafts sections from your inputs and rewrites what you give it, but every section has to be reviewed and approved by you before it counts as done. Results and discussion sections require your own data.
faq.q2: Does it work properly in Arabic?
faq.a2: Yes. The whole interface is right-to-left in Arabic, and the assistant writes in academic Arabic rather than translated English. You can also switch a project's language at any time.
faq.a3: It is built not to. Any citation it suggests is stored as unverified and shown with a warning until you open the source and confirm it. Fabricated DOIs are flagged before they reach you.
faq.q4: Can I come back to a project later?
faq.a4: Every project stores its sections, chat history, notes and references. You reopen it and continue from the exact step you stopped at — on any device.
faq.q5: What happens when I hit the free limit?
faq.a5: Your work is kept. You are asked to upgrade to continue generating, and after upgrading you return to the same step you were on.
faq.a6: Yes, at any time from the billing page. You keep Pro access until the end of the period you already paid for.

error.generic: The file could not be processed.
error.network: Could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
error.noColumns: No columns were found. Check that the first row holds the column names.
error.noRows: The file has no data rows — only column names.
error.notAWorkbook: This could not be read as an Excel workbook. If it is a CSV, save it with a .csv extension; if it is Excel, re-save it from Excel as .xlsx.
error.unreadableWorkbook: The workbook could not be read. It may be damaged or password-protected.

error.tooManyColumns: The file has more columns than can be analysed.
error.legacyXls: This is the older Excel format (.xls), which is not supported. Open it in Excel and save it as .xlsx or .csv, then upload it again.

error.tooFewValues: Too few values ({n}); at least {minimum} are needed.
error.noVariance: The column "{variable}" does not vary — every value is the same, so there is nothing to test.
error.groupTooSmall: One group is too small ({smallest}); at least {minimum} per group are needed.
error.unequalPairs: The two measurements have different lengths ({first} vs {second}).
error.tooFewPairs: Too few complete pairs ({n}); at least {minimum} are needed.
error.noVarianceInDifferences: Every difference is identical, so there is no variance to test.

error.tooFewGroups: ANOVA needs at least two groups of usable size (found {groups}).
error.labelMismatch: The number of groups ({groups}) does not match the number of labels ({labels}).
error.noVariance: There is no variance in the data, so there is nothing to compare.
error.noWithinVariance: There is no variance within the groups.

error.lengthMismatch: The two variables have different lengths ({first} vs {second}).
error.tooFewPairs: Too few complete pairs ({n}); at least {minimum} are needed.
error.constantVariable: The column "{variable}" does not vary, so it cannot correlate with anything.
error.undefined: The correlation could not be computed for this data.
error.tooFewVariables: A correlation matrix needs at least two variables (selected {selected}).
error.duplicateVariable: The same variable cannot be included twice.

error.lengthMismatch: The two variables have different lengths ({first} vs {second}).
error.tooFewLevels: The variable "{variable}" has only {levels} category; at least two are needed.
error.emptyTable: The table is empty — no complete cases.
error.tooFewCategories: At least two categories are needed (found {categories}).
error.labelMismatch: The number of categories ({categories}) does not match the number of labels ({labels}).
error.expectedMismatch: The number of expected proportions ({expected}) does not match the categories ({categories}).
error.proportionsDoNotSumToOne: Expected proportions must sum to 1 (they sum to {sum}).

error.noPredictors: A regression needs at least one predictor.
error.duplicatePredictor: The same predictor cannot be included twice.
error.outcomeAmongPredictors: "{variable}" is both the outcome and a predictor — it cannot predict itself.
error.lengthMismatch: The column "{variable}" has {actual} values but the others have {expected}.
error.tooFewCases: Too few cases ({n}) for {predictors} predictors; at least {minimum} are needed.
error.constantOutcome: The outcome "{variable}" does not vary, so there is nothing to explain.
error.constantPredictor: The predictor "{variable}" does not vary, so it cannot explain anything.
error.perfectCollinearity: One predictor is an exact duplicate of another (or a linear combination of them), so there is no unique solution. Remove the duplicate.

error.tooFewItems: Reliability needs at least two items (selected {selected}).
error.duplicateItem: The same item cannot be included twice.
error.unknownColumn: The column "{column}" is not in this file.
error.notNumericColumn: The column "{column}" is of type "{type}" and cannot be a scale item.
error.nominalColumn: The column "{column}" is categorical and cannot be summed into a total score.
error.noVariance: The total score has no variance, so reliability cannot be computed.

error.shapeMismatch: The matrix dimensions do not match ({left} with {right}).
error.singular: The matrix cannot be inverted — there is a duplicate column or a linear combination.
error.underdetermined: There are fewer rows ({rows}) than columns ({columns}).

error.groupTooSmall: One group is too small ({smallest}); at least {minimum} per group are needed.
error.unequalPairs: The two measurements have different lengths ({first} vs {second}).
error.tooFewPairs: Too few non-zero differences ({n}); at least {minimum} are needed.
error.tooFewGroups: Kruskal-Wallis needs at least three groups (found {groups}). Use Mann-Whitney for two.

error.noPredictors: A logistic regression needs at least one predictor.
error.noCompleteCases: There are no complete cases after removing missing values.
error.outcomeNotBinary: The outcome "{variable}" has {levels} levels; logistic regression needs a binary one.
error.outcomeConstant: The outcome "{variable}" never varies — every case has the same value.
error.tooFewCases: Too few cases ({n}) for {predictors} predictors; at least {minimum} are needed.
error.constantPredictor: The predictor "{variable}" does not vary, so it cannot explain anything.
error.singular: The model could not be fitted — a predictor duplicates another or is a linear combination.

error.tooFewConstructs: The model needs at least two latent constructs (found {constructs}).
error.noPaths: The model has no structural paths; specify the relationships between constructs.
error.unknownIndicator: The indicator "{indicator}" is not in the file (construct "{construct}").
error.sharedIndicator: The indicator "{indicator}" belongs to both "{first}" and "{second}"; an indicator cannot measure two constructs.
error.unknownConstructInPath: A path refers to an undefined construct: "{construct}".
error.cyclicModel: The model contains a cycle ({cycle}); PLS requires a recursive model.
error.tooFewCases: Too few complete cases ({n}); at least {minimum} are needed.
error.constantIndicator: The indicator "{indicator}" does not vary — every response is identical.
error.singularConstruct: Two indicators are identical or one is a linear combination of others, so there is no unique solution.
error.bootstrapUnstable: {failed} of {resamples} resamples failed to converge; the model is too unstable for reliable estimates. Review the indicators and the sample.
error.badOmissionDistance: The omission distance {distance} is outside the accepted range (2 to 20).
error.omissionDistanceDivides: The omission distance {distance} divides the sample size {n} exactly; the same positions would be removed on every pass, so the procedure would not cover the data.

verdict.sound: The measurement model meets the established criteria; nothing requires revision.
verdict.attention: The model is broadly acceptable, with {attention} points worth reviewing before publication.
verdict.problems: There are {problems} issues to address before publication, plus {attention} points to review.

sample.size: The analysis ran on {n} complete cases.
sample.dropped: {dropped} cases ({percent}%) were dropped for missing values on a modelled indicator.
sample.notConverged: The algorithm did not converge; the results are not reliable.

indicator.belowCritical: Indicator "{indicator}" loads at {loading}, below 0.40 — it shares almost nothing with its construct.
indicator.removalWouldFixAve: Indicator "{indicator}" loads at {loading}. AVE is currently {currentAve}; removing this indicator would raise it to {aveIfRemoved}.
indicator.weakButKept: Indicator "{indicator}" loads at {loading}, below 0.708, but keeping it does not breach the other criteria.

ave.met: AVE is {value}; the construct explains {percent}% of the variance in its indicators, establishing convergent validity.
ave.violated: AVE is {value}; the construct explains only {percent}% of the variance in its own indicators, below the 0.50 required for convergent validity.

reliability.met: Composite reliability is {value} (Cronbach's alpha {alpha}), above the 0.70 threshold.
reliability.violated: Composite reliability is {value} (Cronbach's alpha {alpha}), below the 0.70 threshold; the items do not hold together well enough.
reliability.tooHigh: Composite reliability is {value}, above 0.95 — usually a sign of redundant items rather than a better scale.

construct.singleIndicator: This construct has a single indicator, so reliability and convergent validity are undefined for it.

formative.criteria: This is a formative construct: its indicators cause it rather than reflect it, so it is judged by collinearity and weight significance, not by reliability or AVE.
formative.acceptable: No concerning collinearity among the indicators (highest VIF = {value}).
formative.someCollinearity: Collinearity is somewhat elevated (highest VIF = {value}); individual weights are less stable.
formative.collinear: Severe collinearity among the indicators (highest VIF = {value}); individual weights cannot be interpreted with confidence.

htmt.violated: HTMT between {pair} is {value}, above 0.90; the two constructs are not empirically distinct.
htmt.borderline: HTMT between {pair} is {value}, close to the upper bound.

fornellLarcker.violated: Fornell-Larcker fails for "{construct}": the square root of its AVE ({sqrtAve}) is below its correlation with "{with}" ({correlation}).

report.crossLoading: Indicator "{indicator}" correlates more strongly with "{other}" than with its own construct "{own}".

discriminant.allPass: Discriminant validity holds on all three criteria: HTMT, Fornell-Larcker and cross-loadings.

report.rSquared: R² for "{construct}" is {value}; the model explains {percent}% of its variance.

structuralVif.elevated: Collinearity among the predictors of "{construct}" is elevated (VIF = {value}); path coefficients are less stable.
structuralVif.severe: Severe collinearity among the predictors of "{construct}" (VIF = {value}); the path coefficients cannot be interpreted individually.

path.significant: The path {path} is significant: β = {coefficient}, t = {t}, and the confidence interval [{lower}, {upper}] excludes zero.
path.notSignificant: The path {path} is not significant: β = {coefficient}, and the confidence interval [{lower}, {upper}] includes zero.
path.significantButTrivial: The path {path} is statistically significant but its effect is negligible (f² = {fSquared}); removing the predictor barely changes R².

bootstrap.summary: Bootstrapped with {resamples} resamples and {level}% confidence intervals, in {seconds} seconds.
bootstrap.failures: {failed} resamples ({percent}%) failed to converge; a high rate indicates a fragile model.
bootstrap.seed: Random seed {seed}; using it reproduces these results exactly.

action.removeIndicator: Remove "{indicator}" and re-estimate. ⚠️ This is also a theoretical decision: if the item captures an essential facet of the concept, removing it changes what you are measuring.
action.considerRemoving: Consider removing "{indicator}". ⚠️ Read the item first — the numbers cannot see what it measures conceptually.
action.fixAve: To raise AVE: review the weakly loading items, or reconsider how the construct is defined.
action.fixReliability: Review the item wording; low reliability often comes from ambiguity or a reverse-worded item that was not recoded.
action.checkRedundancy: Check the items for repeated meaning; very high reliability with near-identical items is not better measurement.
action.checkMissing: Review the missing data; dropping more than 10% of cases can bias the sample.
action.simplifyModel: Simplify the model or increase the sample size.
action.mergeOrRespecify: Reconsider {pair}: either merge them into one construct, or revise their items so they are theoretically distinct.
action.reviewIndicatorPlacement: Review where "{indicator}" belongs; it may sit better with "{other}".
action.reviewFormativeItems: Review the overlapping items. ⚠️ Removing a formative indicator removes part of the construct's definition, so do not drop it for a high VIF alone.

qSquared.relevant: Predictive relevance for {construct}: Q² = {value}. The model predicts this construct better than its own mean does.
qSquared.notRelevant: Predictive relevance for {construct}: Q² = {value}, at or below zero — the model does not predict this construct better than its mean, however high R² is.

withheld.no-explained-variance: Predictive relevance could not be established for {construct}: the model explains too little of its variance for there to be a prediction to assess. No figure is shown, because any value here would be noise rather than a result.
withheld.insufficient-passes: Predictive relevance could not be established for {construct}: only {passes} blindfolding passes succeeded, too few to rest an estimate on.
withheld.undefined-baseline: Predictive relevance could not be established for {construct}: the baseline sum of squares is zero, so the ratio is undefined.

export.title: PLS-SEM Analysis Report
export.provenance: These results were produced by the standard PLS algorithm and validated against published benchmark results and mathematical properties. They have not been compared against SmartPLS.

data.missingColumns: These columns are not in the file: {columns}.
data.tooFewCases: Only {n} complete cases, below the {minimum} minimum for PLS modelling.
data.fewCasesPerIndicator: Only {ratio} cases per indicator ({n} cases, {indicators} indicators); {recommended} is the usual minimum. Estimates will be less stable.
data.missingData: {dropped} cases ({percent}%) were dropped for missing values on a modelled indicator.
data.zeroVariance: The indicator {columns} does not vary — every respondent gave the same answer, so it cannot correlate with anything. Check whether the question was skipped or the column is a constant left in by an export.
data.binaryIndicator: The indicator {columns} has only two values; it will behave as a category rather than a scale, and its loading is harder to interpret.
data.redundantIndicators: The indicators {columns} correlate at {correlation} within {construct}; they are nearly the same variable, so the weight is split between them arbitrarily.
data.highlyCorrelated: The indicators {columns} correlate at {correlation} within {construct}; their individual weights are less stable.
data.possiblyReverseCoded: The indicator {columns} correlates negatively with the rest of {construct}; it is most likely reverse-worded and not recoded. Recode it before analysing, or reliability collapses for an editorial reason that looks statistical.
data.unknown: A data problem prevents the model from being estimated.

error.interrupted: This analysis stopped because the server restarted. Please run it again.
error.failed: The analysis could not be completed. Check the model and the data, then try again.

error.noConstructs: The model has no latent constructs.
error.tooFewIndicators: {construct} has only {indicators} indicators; confirmatory factor analysis needs at least three per factor, or the model is not identified.
error.tooFewCases: Only {n} cases, below the {minimum} minimum for covariance-based modelling. Use PLS-SEM for smaller samples.
error.constantIndicator: The indicator {indicator} does not vary, so it has no covariance with anything.

warning.few-cases-per-parameter: {ratio} cases per estimated parameter ({n} cases, {parameters} parameters); {recommended} is the usual minimum. Estimates are less stable.
warning.non-normal-indicators: {count} indicators clearly violate normality (worst is {worst}, skew {skew}). Covariance-based modelling assumes multivariate normality; consider PLS-SEM instead.
warning.did-not-converge: Estimation did not converge after {iterations} iterations; the results are not reliable.
warning.heywood-case: {count} negative error variances (a Heywood case); the model is probably misspecified, the sample too small, or an indicator belongs to another factor.

fit.good: Fit is good: the model reproduces the observed covariance matrix closely enough to publish.
fit.acceptable: Fit is acceptable but below the preferred level. Review the weakly loading indicators.
fit.poor: Fit is poor: the model does not reproduce the observed covariance matrix. It should not be published in this form.

warning.small-group: One group has fewer than {threshold} cases, so the result is unstable.
warning.welch-student-disagree: The two forms disagree: Welch p={welchP}, Student p={studentP}. Welch is the reported result.
warning.unequal-groups-and-variances: Group sizes and variances both differ, which makes the classical form unreliable.
warning.normality-violated: The distribution is not normal (W={w}, p={p}) and the sample is small ({n}).
warning.normality-violated-but-large-sample: The normality test is significant, but with {n} cases — above {threshold} — the central limit theorem covers it. You can proceed.
warning.reverse-coded-item: An item appears to be reverse-worded and not recoded. Recode it and run this again.
warning.constant-item: An item has no variance — every respondent gave it the same value.
warning.weak-item: This item correlates below {threshold} with the rest and may measure something else.
warning.small-sample: The sample is small ({n}), so the estimate is unstable.
warning.very-small-sample: The sample is very small ({n}) and the result is not reliable.
warning.two-items-only: Only two items; alpha is unstable in that case.
warning.many-items: There are {k} items, and alpha inflates with scale length.
warning.listwise-deletion: {dropped} of {supplied} rows were dropped for missing values.
warning.heavy-listwise-deletion: {percent}% of rows were dropped for missing values — worth checking your data.
warning.incomplete-pairs-dropped: {dropped} rows were dropped because one of the two measurements was missing.
warning.mixed-item-types: The items are of mixed types ({types}), and alpha assumes one instrument.
warning.unequal-item-spread: Item spreads differ by {ratio}×; use standardised alpha.
warning.possible-redundancy: Alpha is very high ({alpha}), which can mean redundant items rather than a good scale.
warning.negative-alpha: Alpha is negative ({alpha}) — this means a reverse-worded item has not been recoded.
warning.correlation-small-sample: The sample is small ({n}), so the coefficient is unstable.
warning.interval-includes-zero: r={r} but the confidence interval [{lower}, {upper}] includes zero — the relationship may be nothing at all.
warning.pearson-on-non-normal-data: The data are not normally distributed; Spearman fits better here.
warning.spearman-p-approximate: The p-value is approximate at this sample size ({n}).
warning.pairwise-samples-differ: Cells rest on different samples ({minN} to {maxN}) because of missing values.
warning.multiple-comparisons-unadjusted: {comparisons} comparisons with no correction; about {expectedFalsePositives} would be significant by chance alone, and {significantFound} were.
warning.p-values-adjusted: {method} correction applied: {significantBefore} results were significant, {significantAfter} remain.
warning.correlation-cell-unavailable: One correlation could not be computed.
warning.expected-count-below-one: A cell expects fewer than 1 ({minimum}) — the chi-square result is not reliable.
warning.consider-merging-categories: Some categories are sparse. Merging them is a methodological decision for the researcher to review, and the system will not do it automatically.
warning.exact-test-used: Fisher's exact test was used (p={exactP}) because expected counts are small; chi-square would have given {approximateP}.
warning.odds-ratio-corrected-for-zero-cell: The odds ratio ({oddsRatio}) was corrected by adding {adjustment} to each cell because of a zero cell.
warning.severe-multicollinearity: Severe multicollinearity (VIF={worst}) — the coefficients are unstable and cannot be interpreted individually.
warning.residual-autocorrelation: Residuals are correlated (Durbin–Watson={durbinWatson}) — the standard errors are too small.
warning.too-few-cases-per-predictor: Only {ratio} cases per predictor; {recommended} is the usual minimum.
warning.r-squared-inflated-by-predictors: R²={rSquared} but adjusted R²={adjusted} — some of the fit came from having many predictors.
warning.fitted-without-intercept: The model has no intercept; R² is not comparable with ordinary models.
warning.welch-classical-disagree: The two forms disagree: classical p={classicalP}, Welch p={welchP}. Welch is the reported result.
warning.tukey-assumes-equal-variances: Tukey's comparisons assume equal variances, which are violated here; read them with caution.
warning.normality-sample-too-small: The sample is too small to test for normality ({n}).
warning.normality-sample-too-large: The sample is beyond the range of the normality test ({n}).
warning.normality-no-variance: The column has no variance, so its distribution cannot be checked.
warning.homogeneity-not-testable: Equality of variances could not be tested.
warning.ties-corrected: A tie correction was applied across {tiedGroups} groups of repeated values.
warning.zero-differences-dropped: {dropped} zero differences were dropped; the test ran on {remaining} cases.
warning.nonparametric-normal-approximation: The sample is small ({n}); the p-value is a normal approximation.
warning.nonparametric-approximate-due-to-ties: Ties made the exact calculation invalid; the normal approximation was used.
warning.omnibus-needs-posthoc: The result is significant but does not say which groups differ; a post-hoc test is needed.
warning.logistic-separation: Complete separation: a predictor divides the outcome perfectly, so the coefficients cannot be estimated and the odds ratios are meaningless. Remove the predictor or merge its categories.
warning.logistic-too-few-events: Only {events} cases in the smaller outcome group for {predictors} predictors ({ratio} each); at least {recommended} is recommended.
warning.logistic-imbalanced-outcome: The outcome is unbalanced ({percent}%); predicting the majority class alone would score {baseline}%, so accuracy alone is misleading.
